key_insight: Enactor is an actor-centric generative model that enables stable closed-loop microsimulation of signalized intersections by learning vehicle interactions directly, rather than relying on hand-crafted traffic rules or short-horizon predictors.
engineering_relevance: It can produce more realistic intersection-level traffic behavior for simulation, planning, and safety analysis, while better preserving speed, travel-time, and red-light-violation statistics in closed loop.
method: Encodes dynamic vehicles and lane polylines in polar coordinates around the intersection center.
Uses a transformer with separate spatial and temporal attention blocks to predict each actor’s next-step motion distribution.
Trains with a closed-loop curriculum so the model learns to recover from its own generated trajectories.
evidence_signal: Evaluated in 4000-second simulation-in-the-loop tests at two intersection geometries and on real fish-eye camera trajectories, Enactor matched SUMO-like speed and travel-time distributions better than a recent transformer baseline and outperformed a constant-velocity baseline at all forecast horizons.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate intersection-centric context encoding and the closed-loop training setup, so deployment may be sensitive to geometry changes, data quality, or missing actor context.
paper_title: A Generative Model for Closed-Loop Microsimulation of Signalized Intersections
